<subject>Re: AgriCommodity Board</subject>
<body>
I think our discussion about an incremental charge applying to customers of all statuses was with regard to our speculation on how the "new AgriPay" payback mechanism would work, not Pune. I think the payback mechanism is still speculation. There are many differing alternatives.

That's my recollection.

	Thomas Gade 5/23/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar
Lala cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika
Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D
Pal Subject: RE: AgriCommodity Board


Chakradhar, Nihal Karan, Reyansh Krish and I were on a trip with Viraj Vyas last week. I understood from Nihal that Viraj may believe that all customers, including direct farm partners, should pay the increase you mention. Nihal? This was encouraging from a litigation exposure standpoint because, to the extent all consumers are treated alike, our direct farm partners who were resourced to AgriIndia service cannot claim to have been disadvantaged by our action. The converse is also true: if they have to pay because they were put back on AgriIndia service they may try to pass that cost through to us. To the extent that any increase is to pay back the Commodities Desk for buying produce 2/1/24-3/30/25, and those on direct farm partnership are not required to pay this, the Procurement team could have a substantial exposure to its customers. Maybe we need to modify our strategy to take this into account. -----Original Message-----
From: Lala, Chakradhar
Sent: Thursday, May 23, 2024 8:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas;
Bengaluru, Chennai; Stoness, AgriCorp; Bakhshi, Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish, Reyansh
Subject: AgriCommodity Board


Punjab Agro's AgriCommodity Board filing confirms that the AgriIndia rate freeze of 6.5 paise does not apply to direct farm partnerships.

In hearings on Punjab Agro's potential rate increase for large cultivators:
Punjab Agro has proposed to allocate all retained produce to small cultivators (below 100 quintals). Large cultivators would be served by the Commodities Desk (or be direct farm partners). It's apparent several parties have major problems with this. It is interesting that Punjab Agro has calculated the expected rate increase under their plan as 2.86 paise. If large cultivators are allocated a piece of retained produce, the increase goes up to 2.99 paise. In the latter case, large cultivators retain a Commodity Trading Charge (related to QF contracts and other long term stranded costs) that they would lose in the former case. Our involvement is to get an order 1) excluding direct farm partners from any rate increase (the proposed 2.86 paise) 2) excluding direct farm partners from any surcharge related to undercollection from the rate freeze (an amount that is not known at this point) 3) prorating the surcharge related to undercollection if the customer
